title: Training Notes — Billing Error Credits and Respite Conversion Credits on Independent Living Accounts
content:
The rules below govern corrections on Independent Living Residency Agreement ledgers.

**Rule.** A charge posted in error — a wrong amount, a wrong apartment type, a duplicate posting or a fee that does not apply — is corrected only by a billing error credit referencing the exact charge entry being corrected; charges are never deleted. The credit may not exceed the amount of that charge entry less any credits already posted against it, and the correct charge, where one is due, is posted again as a new entry. Each charge entry receives at most one billing error credit. A disputed charge that the records show was correctly posted under the policies of the Independent Living Residency Agreement is not credited.

**Respite conversion credits.** A respite conversion credit is posted only as the consequence of a converted Larkspur trial or respite stay, for the amount the Respite and Short-Term Stay Agreement fixes, carrying the respite stay it comes from; each respite stay yields at most one conversion credit.

## Questions and answers

**Q. A charge of 500.00 already carries a 120.00 credit. What is the most a billing error credit on it may be?**
A. The amount of the entry less credits already posted against it: 500.00 less 120.00, that is 380.00 (hypothetical figures).

**Q. A charge was posted twice. How is the second posting removed?**
A. It is not deleted. A billing error credit referencing the duplicate charge entry corrects it.

**Q. The wrong apartment type's fee was charged. What does the ledger show after correction?**
A. A billing error credit referencing the wrong charge entry, and the correct charge, where one is due, posted again as a new entry.

**Q. A charge entry has already received a billing error credit. Can a second one be posted against it?**
A. No. Each charge entry receives at most one billing error credit.

**Q. The customer disputes a charge that the records show was correctly posted. Is it credited?**
A. No. A disputed charge that the records show was correctly posted is not credited.
